draft.title: Flow maps
card: A flow map uses arrows to show movement between places. Goods, money, people and information can all be mapped.
The arrowhead points to where the movement goes. The tail starts where it comes from.
Thicker arrows show larger flows, and thinner arrows show smaller flows. The legend explains what a given thickness means.
An arrow shows the size and direction of a flow, not the exact route taken. A ship's arrow may be drawn as a straight or curved line.
draft.remember: On a flow map, the arrow shows direction and its thickness shows how large the flow is.

a.q: A flow map of tourists shows a thick arrow from Japan to Queensland and a thin arrow from Japan to Tasmania. What does this show?
opts: More tourists go from Japan to Queensland than to Tasmania
More tourists go from Tasmania to Japan than from Queensland
Tourists to Queensland take a longer route than to Tasmania
Queensland is larger than Tasmania
a.why: Arrow thickness shows the size of the flow, so the thicker arrow means more tourists travel to Queensland. The arrowheads point to Queensland and Tasmania, so the movement is from Japan. Thickness does not show route length or the size of a place.
a.clue: What does a thicker arrow stand for?

b.q: A flow map of iron ore exports shows three arrows leaving Port Hedland. The arrow to China is thickest and the arrow to India is thinnest. Which statement is correct?
opts: Port Hedland sends more ore to China than to India
Port Hedland receives more ore from China than India
India is closer to Port Hedland than China is
China has more iron ore mines than India
b.why: The arrows leave Port Hedland, so the ore moves from there to each place. The thickest arrow to China shows the largest flow. The map does not show distance or the number of mines.
b.clue: Check where the arrows start and which one is thickest.

a.best: More tourists go from Japan to Queensland than to Tasmania

b.best: Port Hedland sends more ore to China than to India

problems.detail: The line 'An arrow shows the size and direction of a flow, not the exact route taken' is stated as true of all flow maps. Some flow maps draw lines that follow real routes, such as shipping lanes through the Suez Canal. It would be safer to say that arrows often do not show the exact route.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. The card overstates that flow map arrows never show the exact route, since some flow maps do follow real routes, and should be softened to 'often'.

card: A flow map uses arrows to show movement between places. Goods, money, people and information can all be mapped.
The arrowhead points to where the movement goes. The tail starts where it comes from.

proposal.remember: On a flow map, the arrow shows direction and its thickness shows how large the flow is.

a.q: A flow map of tourists shows a thick arrow from Japan to Queensland and a thin arrow from Japan to Tasmania. What does this show?
opts: More tourists go from Japan to Queensland than to Tasmania
More tourists go from Tasmania to Japan than from Queensland
Tourists to Queensland take a longer route than to Tasmania
Queensland covers a larger area than Tasmania does
a.why: Arrow thickness shows the size of the flow, so the thicker arrow means more tourists travel to Queensland. The arrowheads point to Queensland and Tasmania, so the movement is from Japan, not towards it. Thickness does not show route length or the size of a place.
a.clue: What does a thicker arrow stand for?

b.q: A flow map of iron ore exports shows three arrows leaving Port Hedland. The arrow to China is thickest and the arrow to India is thinnest. Which statement is correct?
opts: Port Hedland sends more ore to China than to India
Port Hedland receives more ore from China than from India
India is closer to Port Hedland than China is
China has more iron ore mines than India does
b.why: The arrows leave Port Hedland, so the ore moves from there to each place. The thickest arrow, to China, shows the largest flow. Reading the arrows the wrong way round gives the receiving option, and thickness shows flow size, not distance or the number of mines.
b.clue: Check where the arrows start and which one is thickest.
